chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ali ibn Asbat, who said: I said to Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him):
Ibn al-Fudayl ibn Yasar narrated from you and informed us from you about returning to the 'Urras (the place of staying/resting), but we had not stayed there, so we returned to him. What should we do?
He said: 'You pray and lie down for a little while, and indeed Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to pray in it and sit.'
Muammad ibn Ali ibn Fadhl said: 'If I pass through it at a time other than prayer time, after Asr prayer,'
He said: 'It was asked of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about that, and he said: 'Pray in it.''
Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl said to him: 'If you pass through it at night or during the day, do you stay there (make 'Urras), or is the staying only at night?'
He said: 'Yes, if you pass through it at night or during the day, then stay there (make 'Urras), for indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do that.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him)
key_terms.التَّعْرِيسُ: The act of staying overnight or making a temporary residence in a place of worship
key_terms.الْمُعَرَّسِ: The place of staying or resting, specifically referring to the Masjid al-Haram in this context
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on staying overnight in the Masjid al-Haram during the day or night?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of *ta'arrus* (staying overnight or resting) in the Masjid al-Haram, affirming that the practice is not restricted to nighttime but applies to both day and night, following the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). The narration highlights the scholarly transmission chain involving Ibn al-Fudayl and the Imams, emphasizing the continuity of this devotional practice as a means of spiritual retreat and prayer within the sacred precincts.
